title: Installing a Second Sink in a Bath Vanity: hole cutting, drainage, and faucet hookup
summary: The video demonstrates adding a second sink to an existing bath vanity. It begins with positioning the new sink and using the manufacturer's template to mark the cutout, including a pilot hole for a jigsaw. It then shows rough-in work: cutting into the PVC for the drain, routing a drain branch back to the existing lavatory, and upgrading to copper shut-offs with a copper tee for separate service, all secured with bell hangers. The final segment covers trimming out the sink: installing the faucet (spout, handles, and pop-up stopper), applying plumber’s putty and thread sealant, caulking around the sink edge, and connecting braided stainless steel supply lines, ensuring the assembly fits within the existing vanity setup.

pilot hole technique for jigsaw insertion
sections.description: The installer places the new sink in a similar position to the existing one, references the sink's template to mark the cutout, and drills a pilot hole to guide the jigsaw for creating the opening.

sections.title: Rough-in: drain layout, copper supply, and independent shut-offs
sections.description: After marking the opening, the video covers dry-fitting the drain and routing a branch to the existing sink, installing a trap adapter, and upgrading supply lines with copper tees and separate shut-offs, all secured with bell hangers.

sections.title: Trim-out: faucet installation, stopper, and final connections
concepts: spout, handles, and pop-up stopper assembly
thread sealing compound on faucet threads
sections.description: The final section covers completing the sink installation: mounting the faucet with putty and sealant, adjusting the pop-up stopper linkage, caulking the sink edge, and connecting hot and cold braided supply lines while checking for fit and clearance.
